Definition of done:
- `RenewDue` claims each subscription's period in the store before it invoices, so concurrent or repeated calls create and charge at most one invoice per subscription and period. When the gateway is unavailable, the period still advances, the invoice stays open, and the status is kept. A failing subscription no longer stops the others, and the errors are returned together.
- New tests in `internal/subscriptions` cover concurrent `RenewDue` calls (one invoice, one charge), repeated calls with the gateway down (one invoice, period advanced, status kept), and one failing subscription not blocking the rest.
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

Approach: the claim is a compare-and-set under the store lock. Only the call that moves the period from the one it read to the next gets to invoice. Everyone else sees a moved period and skips it. Invoicing happens after the claim, so a crash can skip a period but never invoice it twice.

Now the change to `renew`, splitting invoice creation from payment so the outage case can be handled separately.

- `RenewDue` claims each subscription's period in the store before it invoices, so concurrent or repeated calls create and charge at most one invoice per subscription and period. When the gateway is unavailable, the period still advances, the invoice stays open, and the status is kept. A failing subscription no longer stops the others, and the errors are returned together.
- New tests in `internal/subscriptions` cover concurrent `RenewDue` calls (one invoice, one charge), repeated calls with the gateway down (one invoice, period advanced, status kept), and one failing subscription not blocking the rest.
- `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

Approach: the claim is a compare-and-set under the store lock. Only the call that moves the period from the one it read to the next gets to invoice. Everyone else sees a moved period and skips it. Invoicing happens after the claim, so a crash can skip a period but never invoice it twice.

Now the change to `renew`, splitting invoice creation from payment so the outage case can be handled separately.

The stale-read test failed because of a one-line bug in `claim` (`internal/subscriptions/subscriptions.go:238`). `claim` set a `moved` flag when another call had already moved the period on, but the return check was `if err != nil || (moved && false)`, so the moved case was still reported as claimed. A stale `renew` then went on to create and charge a second invoice for the same period.

The fix is `if err != nil || moved {`. Now a call that finds its period already moved returns `false` and changes nothing.
